title: test-0016-SCI-CHM-MATERIALS
passage: Today in our science lab, we explored how different materials behave when placed in water or light. First, we took a large wooden log and a tiny wooden splinter, placing both into a bucket of water. Both items floated, proving that density, not just size or weight, determines if an object sinks. Next, we stirred a spoonful of sugar into a glass of water. The sugar seemed to vanish, but it did not turn into water; it simply broke into tiny particles that spread evenly throughout the liquid, creating a solution. We then tested a piece of clear glass and a dark-colored plastic sheet. The glass allowed light to pass through, but even clear glass blocks a small amount of light, which is why we see faint reflections. Finally, we examined a shiny metal spoon and a polished piece of plastic. We learned that lustre is a natural property of the material's surface, not a paint or coating applied later. We also observed that some liquids, like oil and water, do not mix at all, even though both are fluids. This experiment helped us understand that materials have unique properties that define how they interact with their environment.
